participating-org.narrative:
1.HISTORY
African Women Agri-business Network Uganda Ltd (AWAN) is a membership organization that focuses on advancing the socio-economic status of women through the promotion of gender-inclusive Agri-food value chains.
The organization has 250 members, all women entrepreneurs operating in agri-food value chains. AWAN’s mission is to provide women-owned agribusinesses with a platform that facilitates improved production, access to markets, trade information, blended and inclusive finance, innovative technology, and the opportunity to share success stories and experiences. AWAN has worked with over 300 women-founded enterprises and 20000 smallholder farmers to access financial and non-financial business development services such as certification, export readiness, product development, formalization, establishing out-grower schemes, and business coaching and mentorship. AWAN offers various pieces of training in branding and packaging, market-entry, business operations, financial modeling, finance readiness, business planning, bookkeeping, and standardization.
2. ACHIEVEMENTS
1. AWAN has reached 20000 smallholder farmers with a range of interventions including linkages to formal markets, access to quality farm inputs, training in good agricultural practices, access to post-harvest handling skills and materials, financial and digital services. 2. Supported 560 MSMEs including members and non-member MSMEs to access financing, technologies for agro-processing, formal local, regional and international markets, workspace, mentorship and customised trainings. 3.Built the membership to 300 SMEs all women led/owned MSMEs. 4. Developed working relationships with reputable local and international actors such as Danchurch Aid, GIZ, Trade Facilitation Office Canada, Graca Machel Trust, Private Sector Foundation Uganda, UgandaExport Promotions Board, Stanbic Bank, DFCU Bank and Gudie Leisure Farm.
3. INSTITUTIONAL PURPOSE Mission: Economic Empowerment ofWomen through building gender and nutrition-sensitive value chains.
Institutional objectives: 1. Building the capacity of women and young girls to access economic opportunities and jobs in Agri-food value chains. 2. Increasing access to finance and non-financialbusiness development services. 3. Enabling women and young girls to access formal lucrative markets in agriculture value chains. 4.Advocating for gender-inclusive legal and policy environment.
3. STRATEGIC POSITIONING
AWAN is an Entrepreneurship Support Organisation (ESO) focusing on building the capacity of women-owned SMEs operating within the agri-food value chains. AWAN operates in an entrepreneurship ecosystem that involves main actors including smallholder farmers, entrepreneurs/MSMEs, financial institutions, regulatory bodies such as URA, URSB, UNBS, and development organizations. All these actors are important in ensuring that agri-food value chains work for women as entrepreneurs or smallholder farmers/producers. AWAN as an ESO occupies a unique position at the intersection bringing together the demand and supply actors within the agri-food market system. We support women MSMEs to access essential functions such as financing, formalization, compliance with tax and other statutory obligations, support with certificationand others. We also work with the SMEs to develop sustainable and gender-inclusive supply chains through out-grower schemes.
